I would like clarification regarding the Business Entity Resolution Challenge.

I understand that the task is to identify matching business records across Source 1, Source 2, and Source 3 using the provided training data. I would like to confirm the recommended approach for candidate generation/blocking and final matching, especially when one Source 1 entity can match multiple records from Source 2 and/or Source 3.

I would also like to confirm whether standard ML libraries such as scikit-learn and LightGBM, along with Jaccard similarity, Levenshtein distance, and TF-IDF cosine similarity, are permitted when using only the provided challenge data and no external APIs, databases, geocoding services, or external business information.

Response from Amazon Leaders:
One Source 1 entity may match many Source 2/3 records.
 
 Your solution must not inject external data. Prohibited: external databases, APIs, geocoding/entity lookup, internet-sourced augmentation, and packages bundling external geo/postal/business data (e.g. libpostal, geocoders, postal-code or gazetteer datasets). Allowed: pure-algorithm libraries (e.g. RapidFuzz, jellyfish, scikit-learn, LightGBM, pandas), general-language pretrained NLP/embedding models within the limits, any algorithm using only the provided records, and small hand-written normalization dictionaries.

Are publicly available pretrained models (e.g., open-source sentence embedding models like MiniLM, or other Hugging Face models) allowed for feature extraction or as part of the solution pipeline?

Pretrained open-weight models are allowed if MIT/Apache-2.0 licensed, up to 8B params, run offline, and fine-tuned only on the provided data. Hosted LLM APIs (Claude/Gemini/ChatGPT) are not allowed.

The packages shouldn't inject external data. Prohibited: external databases, APIs, geocoding/entity lookup, internet-sourced augmentation, and packages bundling external geo/postal/business data (e.g. libpostal, geocoders, postal-code or gazetteer datasets, large static country/state/city tables). Allowed: pure-algorithm libraries (e.g. RapidFuzz, jellyfish, scikit-learn, pandas), general-language pretrained NLP/embedding models within the limits (e.g. fastText, wordfreq fine), any algorithm using only the provided records, and small hand-written normalization dictionaries.

Yes, AI coding assistants are allowed.

Issue Description:
When attempting to submit the matching_results.tsv file on the competition portal (/competitions/1743604/round/1593683/play/code), the submission dialog gets permanently stuck on "Please Wait (0)", and the file is never uploaded to S3.

Upon inspecting Developer Tools (Network & Console), we identified the exact root cause:

Root Cause Analysis (Technical Details):
Missing Windows MIME Type for .tsv: In Windows (Chrome / Edge / Chromium browsers), the .tsv file extension has no default registered MIME type in the OS registry. As a result, the HTML5 File API evaluates file.type as an empty string "".

Backend API Rejection: When submitting, the portal triggers:

Endpoint: POST /api/code-contest/create-presigned-url-for-upload-ml-submission
Request Payload:
json


{
  "codeContest": 290344,
  "file_name": "matching_results.tsv",
  "file_type": ""
}
Because file_type is an empty string "", the backend server rejects the request with HTTP 400:

json


{
  "status": false,
  "data": {
    "url": "",
    "file": "matching_results.tsv"
  },
  "message": "Bad Request"
}
